# Lightweight Local Web UI for CLI-Backed Tools

Best practices for building a local-only web application that serves as a conversational
UI for command-line tools. The app receives user input via a browser, dispatches work to
a CLI subprocess (e.g., `claude -p`), and renders the CLI's markdown output as styled HTML.
Research covers 6 dimensions with 34 verified sources.

## Recommended Stack

| Layer | Choice | Key Reason |
|-------|--------|------------|
| Backend | FastAPI | Native async + built-in SSE (v0.135.0+) |
| Transport | SSE | Unidirectional, auto-reconnect, proxy-friendly |
| Subprocess | asyncio.create_subprocess | Non-blocking StreamReader |
| Markdown | marked.js (client-side) | 2x faster than markdown-it; streaming-compatible |
| Code highlighting | highlight.js | 15.6 KiB; auto-detection; active maintenance |
| Mermaid | Lazy-loaded CDN | 2.69 MB bundle -- load only when diagram detected |
| Frontend | htmx + SSE extension | Under 200 LOC for streaming chat; no build step |
| System tray | Skip | Terminal command is simpler; avoids GNOME extension dep |
| Security | TrustedHostMiddleware + 127.0.0.1 | DNS rebinding is a real threat (CVE-2025-49596) |

## Quick Decision Framework

1. **Async subprocess streaming needed?** Yes -> FastAPI (not Flask)
2. **Streaming direction?** Server-to-client -> SSE (not WebSocket)
3. **Markdown rendering?** Client-side (streaming + Mermaid need browser DOM)
4. **Build step OK?** No -> htmx + CDN libraries
5. **Tray icon?** No (developer audience, GNOME extension fragility)
6. **"It's just localhost" = safe?** No -- bind 127.0.0.1, validate Host header
